summary: Large jobs import, compile and pass post preflight without quadratic slowdowns. Contour analysis links intersection diagnostics to chains through one grouping pass instead of scanning every intersection for every chain, and path elements dedupe diagnostic ids with a set. Controller compensation is resolved against one document-wide topology lookup per compile instead of rebuilding the segment map and rescanning chains, contours and diagnostics for every operation, and the every-operation compensation preflight uses a set of compensated operations instead of a nested event scan. A custom post run stopped by a resource limit (including the wall-clock deadline) now reports POST_CUSTOM_RESOURCE_LIMIT instead of POST_CUSTOM_NONDETERMINISTIC when the other determinism run finished.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. Imported documents, execution plans and posted programs are byte-identical. One diagnostic changes: when only one of the two isolated determinism runs hits a resource limit (typically the 1 s wall-clock deadline under machine load), the post now fails with POST_CUSTOM_RESOURCE_LIMIT instead of POST_CUSTOM_NONDETERMINISTIC, and a first run stopped by a resource limit is no longer repeated. Both outcomes were and remain failures; no resource limit value changed.

checklist.schema: No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, CAD, storage or journal schema change. Post engine API remains 1; saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, WebMCP tool, cancellation or input-version behavior change.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. compensationRequiredForEveryOperation reports the same diagnostics for the same plans.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change. Custom post failures stopped by a resource limit report POST_CUSTOM_RESOURCE_LIMIT, which the event diagnostic catalog already documents; documented limit values are unchanged.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change.
checklist.verification: Imported UPID documents hash identically before and after across 1,600 randomized drawings (near-origin and randomized tolerances). Execution plans plus per-operation compensation resolution, eligibility and suggestions hash identically across 1,800 randomized drawings (default, randomized tolerances and clean part layouts). New tests cover intersection-diagnostic linking growth and correctness for 2,000 and 8,000 crossing chains; a shared topology lookup giving the same result as per-operation resolution for ready, intersecting, diagnostic-blocked and open operations; the every-operation compensation preflight with one compensated and one centerline operation in either order; and determinism reconciliation when either run hits a resource limit. Contour analysis of 16,000 crossing line pairs went from 12.8 s to 0.13 s, and a fuzzed 2,300-chain block array with 232,367 intersections planned in 6 s instead of 49 s. Compile time for 250/500/2,000 parts went from 201/648/28,781 ms to 111/154/544 ms; preflight on 16,251 events went from 294 ms to 2 ms. The pure-domain suite, browser domain, editor and WebMCP suites, tsc -b and npm run lint pass.

publicNotes.summary: Large drawings import and compile much faster, and posts that run out of time say so.
changes: Importing a drawing with thousands of separate paths that cross each other no longer slows down with the square of the path count.
Building the execution plan for a job with thousands of contours takes well under a second instead of growing with the square of the contour count.
Checking a machine post against a large execution plan no longer slows down with the number of events.
When a post stops because it hit its time or memory limit, the error now names the resource limit instead of saying the post produced different results on two runs.
publicNotes.compatibility: Imported projects, execution plans and posted programs are unchanged. Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and CAD files are unchanged.
